title: Chvátal's degree condition for a Hamilton path
statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph on $
u \ge 2$ vertices, with degrees arranged in nondecreasing order as $d_1 \le d_2 \le \cdots \le d_
u$. Suppose there is no integer $m$ with $1 \le m < (
u+1)/2$ for which both $d_m < m$ and $d_{
u-m+1} < 
u - m$. Then $G$ has a Hamilton path, that is, a path that passes through every vertex of $G$ exactly once. (Chvátal)
hypotheses_covered: the graph is finite with at least two vertices ($\nu \ge 2$)
replaced:
Ex 4.2.4*: Chv\'atal's Hamilton-path degree condition (counting form).

4.2.4* Let $G$ be a nontrivial simple graph with degree sequence $(d_1, d_2, \ldots,
d_\nu)$, where $d_1 \leq d_2 \leq \ldots \leq d_\nu$. Show that if there is no value of
$m$ less than $(\nu+1)/2$ for which $d_m < m$ and $d_{\nu-m+1} < \nu - m$, then $G$ has
a Hamilton path. (V. Chv\'atal)
